arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The applicant stated the city approved 284 flags without denial. The applicant argued the city targeted the word Christian specifically.
The city argued it uses its property for lawful expressive purposes. The city claimed it is not compelled to express competing viewpoints.
Justice Kavanaugh asked if the city could ban anti-American flags. He asked if the city could reject flags supporting discrimination.
The city argued it can select the views it wants to express. The city claimed this control is a core aspect of government speech.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether a city can treat its flagpole as a government speech platform. If so, the city controls the message. If not, it must treat all speakers equally.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The applicant wants the city to treat the flagpole as a public forum. This would force the city to accept all lawful flags.
The city wants the court to treat the flagpole as government speech. This would let the city choose which messages to display.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The applicant argues the city acted as a neutral host. It cannot reject a flag because of its religious viewpoint.
The city argues it controls its own property. It may select the views it wishes to express on its flagpole.
